anchors.paper_title: Development and Evaluation of a Smartphone-Based Electroencephalography (EEG) System
anchors.reason: Describes design and evaluation of a smartphone-based 19-channel EEG hardware system (ADS1299), a technical tool, not a description of this arithmetic workload dataset.

metadata.methods_description: EEG was recorded with a mobile system using a 19-channel 10-20 montage (Ag/AgCl electrodes, linked-ear reference, 250 Hz), together with 3-lead ECG on the same system and Pupil Labs Pupil Core eye tracking, synchronized via LSL. After a 60 s baseline, participants answered 70 arithmetic questions (10 per difficulty level), each presented for 6 s in randomized order.

citation_details.title: Benchmarking Multimodal Workload Classification: Effects of Modality, Validation Protocol, and Segmentation Contrast on an Open Graded-Arithmetic Dataset
citation_details.author: Liam Booth, Adeel Mehmood, Mehdi Zeinali
citation_details.abstract: Physiology-based mental workload classification is hard to compare across studies because task design, preprocessing, segmentation, and validation protocols vary widely. Using OpenNeuro ds007262, an open multimodal arithmetic dataset of synchronised 19-channel 10-20 system electroencephalography (EEG), electrocardiography (ECG), and pupillometry data from 18 released participants (16 retained after participant-level quality control for downstream modelling) spanning seven objective difficulty bands plus baseline fixation, we present a reproducible end-to-end machine learning pipeline for graded workload classification. The pipeline standardises participant-level quality control, trial-aligned windowing, modality-specific preprocessing and feature extraction (153 EEG, 18 ECG, and 25 pupillometry features), and supervised evaluation under three validation protocols (within-participant, pooled-stratified, and group-holdout) over eleven models and five class scenarios. Fused representations generally performed best; EEG was the strongest unimodal modality, and classical models outperformed deep models in most feature-based conditions. The best 6 s pipeline reached a balanced accuracy of 0.635; under denser 3 s overlap segmentation, the best pipeline reached 0.718. Mean balanced accuracy across 60 matched cells rose from 0.324 to 0.380, with gains concentrated in within-participant and pooled-stratified evaluation rather than strict unseen-participant transfer. The pipeline provides a transparent benchmark framework for fine-grained physiological workload modelling.

citation_details.title: Predicting Cognitive Tasks from Single-Channel EEG through Task-Semantic Alignment
citation_details.author: Ryota Kanai C
citation_details.abstract: Studies of data scaling in electroencephalography (EEG) and related noninvasive recordings suggest that simple wearable devices could eventually reveal more about cognitive states. However, publicly available EEG data are difficult to combine. Different laboratories record different tasks, participants, and devices. Task-agnostic self-supervised learning can exploit such data, but representations learned only with EEG signals have not consistently produced feature representations that are directly effective for decoding the cognitive state. We therefore aimed to incorporate task information by embedding experimental instructions, stimuli and response demands in a common semantic space, and trained an EEG encoder to align signals from a single anterior--posterior differential channel with those task vectors. This framework supports zero-shot prediction without target-condition calibration and few-shot prediction using labeled samples. On a reserved ten-class evaluation, the highest observed zero-shot balanced accuracy was 30.13% (chance 10%). In a separate developmental few-shot experiment, balanced accuracy reached 34.47% using 16 labeled EEG examples per class from another participant, and 74.99% using examples from the test participant's own task recording. Our experiments suggest that training models on datasets with multiple tasks per participant appeared useful, whereas adding datasets containing only one or a few tasks sometimes reduced established performance despite broader task coverage. These exploratory results suggest that EEG datasets that repeat varied cognitive tasks and everyday activities within the same individuals across days, devices and independent studies would be particularly useful for training an EEG foundation model for predicting cognitive states.
